parties: Acquirer: Standex International Corporation (NYSE:SXI); Sellers: Amran, LLC (operating as Amran Instrument Transformers) and Narayan Powertech Private Limited, including Shah family shareholders
headline: Standex acquires US and India transformer makers for $462M landmark two-stage deal, largest in company history.
sum: Standex International completed its largest acquisition ever—a parallel cross-border deal acquiring 100% of US-based Amran Instrument Transformers (85% cash, 15% stock) and India-based Narayan Powertech (90.1% initially for ~$262M cash at first closing, then final 9.9% for ~$64M cash at second closing in July 2026). The transaction, structured via Standex's Singapore subsidiary Mold-Tech, was subject to RBI regulatory approval and triggered Indian FX, competition, and tax analysis.
implication: A two-stage closing structure with FX-linked regulatory gates—particularly the RBI 10% stock consideration holdback dependent on foreign exchange approvals—exemplifies how cross-border deal counsel sequences documentation, closings, and shareholder rights termination across parallel US and Indian regulatory windows.
detail: <cite index="20-2,20-4,20-5,20-6">Standex acquired 100% of Amran at the US level and, through its wholly owned Singapore subsidiary Mold-Tech Singapore Pte. Ltd., acquired 90.1% of Narayan at the India level in simultaneous transactions announced at a combined enterprise value of approximately $462 million.</cite> <cite index="20-7">The consideration for Amran comprised 85% cash and 15% Standex common stock, while the initial acquisition of 90.1% of Narayan was completed for cash consideration of approximately $262 million.</cite> <cite index="20-8,22-1">At second closing on July 2, 2026, Mold-Tech acquired the remaining 9.9% interest in Narayan for approximately $64 million in cash.</cite> <cite index="15-6,15-7">The 10% share exchange related to Narayan Powertech was subject to India regulatory approval, expected to take up to six months.</cite> <cite index="3-2">The transaction gave Standex full ownership of Narayan and terminated minority shareholder rights and the prior shareholders' agreement without penalty.</cite>

structure.novel: Two-stage simultaneous closing with parallel US (100% Amran) and India (90.1% Narayan) transactions; second closing mechanic for minority 9.9% squeeze-out in India dependent on RBI FX approval of original stock consideration, structured via Singapore inbound SPV to optimize tax and regulatory treatment. Termination of shareholders' agreement and minority put/call options without penalties upon second closing.

triggers.law: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA) and RBI Regulations
triggers.note: FX approval gate for 10% stock consideration in Narayan; inbound investment by Mold-Tech Singapore (non-resident entity); deemed inbound FDI in share acquisition.

Combination notification required pre-completion for acquisition of control over Narayan (where Standex acquires ≥25% voting rights). Deal size (~$326M India portion) likely triggers reportability thresholds.
Capital gains taxation on sellers; withholding tax at source on purchase consideration; transfer pricing documentation for allocations between US and India entities.

triggers.note: Board and shareholder approval for Narayan selling parties; compliance with disclosure norms in share purchase agreements.
